118-M000133.writeup: Senator Edward Markey's record in the 118th Congress shows a significant recent shift on the anchor issue of aid to Israel, where he voted against emergency aid packages and discharge petitions in 2023 and 2024, breaking with the majority of his party. However, this recent consistency is undermined by his earlier votes in 2010 and 2012 supporting Israel loan guarantees and assistance, indicating a late turn rather than a lifelong principle. In the area of military aid to other countries, Markey is inconsistent; while he voted against the Ukraine supplemental in 2022, he voted against limiting aid in 2023 and against discharging resolutions that would have restricted aid, showing a lack of firm anti-interventionist stance. His record on sanctions is heavily interventionist, with only 2 of 18 votes against sanctions, suggesting he supports the use of economic pressure as a tool of foreign policy. On war authorizations, Markey voted to repeal the 2001 and 2002 AUMFs in 2023, a strong anti-interventionist signal, but he also voted against amendments that would have narrowed or delayed the termination of these powers, creating a mixed record. His votes on the use of force abroad are similarly mixed, with strong anti-interventionist votes on Iran-related resolutions in 2020 and 2024, but interventionist votes on broader defense appropriations and force authorizations in other contexts. The combination of a recent but late turn on Israel, inconsistent votes on military aid and sanctions, and a mixed record on war powers suggests Markey is a political actor who aligns with anti-interventionist positions when politically advantageous or when the party consensus shifts, rather than a reliable principled ally. He does not meet the floor for a hard ally due to the lack of consistency across all five areas and the late timing of his most significant anti-interventionist votes.
